questions.question: What is a sitar?
choices: A plucked string instrument associated with South Asian musical traditions

questions.question: The kora is traditionally associated with which region?
What type of instrument is a djembe?
The shakuhachi is a Japanese instrument in which family?
What is a didgeridoo traditionally made from?
choices: A hollowed branch or tree trunk
A stretched hide over a frame

questions.question: Which instrument is strongly associated with Andean music?
What is the erhu?
choices: A two-string bowed instrument from China

questions.question: The koto is a Japanese instrument commonly described as what?
What is a mbira?
choices: A lamellophone with metal keys attached to a board or resonator

questions.question: How can a musician study an instrument respectfully across cultures?
choices: Treat it as an ancient object with no current players
Learn its community context, names, uses, and living traditions
Assume every region uses it identically

questions.question: Which instrument is associated with Scottish musical traditions?
What is a gamelan?
choices: An Indonesian ensemble featuring tuned gongs and other instruments

questions.question: What is a balalaika?
choices: A Russian plucked string instrument with a triangular body

questions.question: The tabla is best described as what?
choices: A pair of tuned hand drums used in South Asian music

questions.question: What does instrument timbre depend on?
choices: Sound source, materials, shape, and performance technique

questions.question: Why may the same instrument have different roles in different musical traditions?
choices: Every instrument has one universal role
Instrument design determines a single genre
Musical roles and techniques depend on local practices and contexts

questions.question: What is a balafon?
choices: A West African wooden keyed percussion instrument

questions.question: How is the shamisen commonly played?
choices: With a bow on a single string
With a large plectrum on a three-string instrument

questions.question: A class hears a recording of an unfamiliar instrument. Which approach supports careful identification?
choices: Guess only from the recording title
Assume it comes from the nearest country
Compare its sound and playing method with reliable cultural context

questions.question: Why should a world-music lesson include living artists and communities?
choices: It limits listening to old recordings
It presents traditions as active, varied, and shaped by people today
